title: Lohri, and the fire that carries gifts
hook: a winter bonfire, a fistful of sesame and popcorn, and a song about an outlaw
carry: agni carries what we give to god
tomorrow: who gets the first of the harvest?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the mother feeds everyone who comes: Shridhar's feast, and a jagran with the whole lane invited.

Cold enough to see your breath. A courtyard in Punjab, and in the middle, a bonfire taller than the kids around it. Someone presses a handful into your palm: sesame seeds, peanuts, a little hard sweet called rewri, a few pieces of popcorn. Everyone walks around the fire and throws a pinch in. The flames jump. Earlier, children went door to door singing, and came home with sweets and coins. The song is about an outlaw. Today, Lohri. Back on day one hundred fifty-two it got one line; today it gets the whole fire.
screen: `A BONFIRE IN THE COLD.` → `SESAME AND POPCORN IN THE PALM.` → `A SONG ABOUT AN OUTLAW.`

segments.voice: Lohri comes in the deep of winter, on the night before Maghi, the day tradition counts as the start of the sun's northward journey. First, the fire, and one of Hinduism's oldest teachings. The very first word of the Rig Veda, the oldest Hindu scripture, is Agni: fire. Its first hymn praises Agni as the priest who carries offerings to the gods. Whatever is poured into the fire, Agni takes up. At Lohri there's no priest and no chanting required, just a family tossing sesame and grain into the flames, some bowing as they go around. But the teaching is the same one: give to the fire, and the fire carries it to God. It's the same Agni who witnesses a Hindu wedding, as the couple walks around him. Then, the people. Lohri belongs to the Punjabi year itself, so Hindus, Sikhs and their neighbors keep it, each in their own way. It's loudest for a family with a first: a new baby's first Lohri, a new bride's first Lohri in her husband's home. The family's newest gift is brought to the fire with thanks. Then, the song. Children go door to door singing about Dulla Bhatti, a Punjabi Muslim folk hero remembered as an outlaw who, the story says, rescued a poor girl and saw her married as if she were his own daughter. So around a Hindu household's fire, kids sing about a Muslim outlaw with a good heart. Each family brings its own prayers, and the same heat reaches every face.
screen: `THE NIGHT BEFORE MAGHI` · `THE RIG VEDA'S FIRST WORD: AGNI` · `THE FIRE CARRIES THE OFFERING` · `A WELCOME FOR EACH NEW FIRST` · `A SONG FOR DULLA BHATTI`

segments.voice: Cup one hand in your lap as if it holds sesame and popcorn, and think of one thing from this season you'd gladly give to the fire: a worry, a grudge, a tiredness carried too long. Hold it for a few breaths, then open the hand on an out-breath; if you pray, offer it to God, or to Agni, as the fire does.
Punjab's shared devotional ground. Today, Lohri, the winter fire on the night before Maghi, with sesame given to Agni and a song for Dulla Bhatti. Today's word.
Your line: agni carries what we give to god. For a new baby or a new bride, the bonfire is a thank-you. I'll be here tomorrow.
